# The Marin data-quality classifier: what it is, how it was trained and evaluated, and whether the weights can be shared

## TL;DR

- **The "data classifier"** is the datakit **document-quality classifier**. The one actually **deployed** at the 2026-07-16 freeze is **fastText v0, run `sonnet46-thr05`**, tracked in [marin-community/marin#5810](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5810) (child of the May quality-scores one-pager [#5360](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5360)). It scores every active Datakit source with `attributes.high_score = P(high) ∈ [0,1]`, distilled from a **claude-sonnet-4-6** 1–5 pretraining-utility rubric. Held-out (n=961): **AUC 0.846 / Spearman ρ 0.641** (achieved), API spend **$32.73** (< $50 cap).
- It has **three generations**, of which only the first is deployed:
  1. **fastText v0 `sonnet46-thr05`** ([#5810](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5810), rav) — **deployed** at `experiments/datakit/cluster/quality/v0`.
  2. **pooled fast-transformer** ([#6739](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6739) / PR [#6741](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6741), rjpower) — **AUC 0.875 / ρ 0.703** on the *same* oracle labels; a **recommendation, never wired into the inference path**, decision left pending.
  3. **calibrated "coherent quality" relabel** ([#6849](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6849), [#6860](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6860), RFC PR [#7040](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/7040), rav) — an **open RFC posted 2026-07-10**, on branch `rav/quality-coherence`, **not merged, not deployed**.
- **Critical evaluation caveat (the state-of-the-art view at freeze):** the celebrated oracle-AUC is now considered a **confounded metric**. Source identity alone predicts the oracle at **AUC 0.852** (η² = 0.41), *above* fastText's 0.846 and only ~0.023 below the fast-transformer's 0.875 — so most of the "win" is recovering domain/source signal, not intrinsic quality. The team's own conclusion: "**raising oracle-AUC does not fix**" the real problem.
- **Weight sharing:** **no explicit release decision exists in the corpus** (gap). But Marin's revealed behavior is **default-open** — it already published this classifier's *debugging report* to the world-readable `gs://marin-public`, keeps its data pool public on HuggingFace, routinely releases model weights, and builds on AllenAI's openly-released `dolma3-fasttext-quality-classifier`. The only genuine (but **undiscussed-as-a-blocker**) constraint is that the labels are distilled from Claude outputs.

---

## 1. What the model is — and which generation is actually live

### Generation 1 — fastText v0 `sonnet46-thr05` (DEPLOYED)

The classifier's stated job ([#5810 body](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5810)): "Train a fastText quality classifier whose labels come from an LLM oracle scoring documents against a written rubric, and apply it across every active Datakit source as `attributes.high_score = P(high) ∈ [0, 1]` — co-partitioned with normalized parquet so it slots into the existing `classify_fasttext_step` consumer shape (drop-in alongside dolma3-quality)."

v0 design choices ([#5810](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5810)): **a single rubric across all sources**, a **binary** fastText model (label = "rubric ≥ Average") that emits **`P(high)` as a continuous score** at inference, and it lands as a **parallel attribute** — explicit v0 non-goals were per-domain rubrics, a multi-class/regression head, threshold tuning, and *replacing* dolma3-quality in the mixture. The deployed run is **`sonnet46-thr05`** ([#5810 run comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5810#issuecomment-4480271122)). It feeds the store as one axis of **quality (5 buckets) × domain (40 luxical-one clusters) = 200 tokenized buckets** at `gs://marin-eu-west4/datakit/store/v0.1_20260518` ([#5360 comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5360#issuecomment-4483228852)).

**v0 is deliberately provisional.** rav, #data-mixing, **2026-06-29**: "keep in mind that **both domain and quality classifiers are v0** — the goal was to have e2e pipeline. We can definitely do better!" ([Discord](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1462895580064911522/1521206652320223323)). The v0 label and this quote reframe the whole model as an intentionally-first-pass artifact, not a finished production system.

### Generation 2 — pooled fast-transformer (RECOMMENDED, NOT DEPLOYED)

[#6739](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6739) (PR [#6741](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6741), rjpower, agent thread "weaver #329") tested whether a small `embed → pool@64 → transformer → regression-head` model could beat the deployed fastText under a <1M FLOPs/token budget, **reusing the exact same Sonnet-4.6 train/eval splits and the same `eval_holdout.py` harness**. The winner (meanmaxmin·w64·d512·L4, 32M params) reached **AUC 0.875 / ρ 0.703 at 0.41M FLOPs/token** ([final report](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6739#issuecomment-4826633470)).

This win was **never adopted into the inference path**. The plan's Phase 3 was "*(if it wins)* wire it into the v0 inference path" ([#6739 body](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6739)), but the last substantive comment (2026-06-29) leaves it explicitly undecided: "**Decision point:** (a) ship the current pooled model as the deliverable win over fasttext, and/or (b) approve a targeted Sonnet-oracle spend … Holding for direction before any spend." ([state comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6739#issuecomment-4833334278)). "Adopt the meanmaxmin model over fasttext" is **rjpower's own recommendation in the report, not an adoption record**. The July bug reports ([#6849](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6849), [#6860](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6860)) still target `quality/v0` — confirming the fast-transformer was never the live classifier.

### Generation 3 — the calibrated "coherent quality" relabel (OPEN RFC, NOT DEPLOYED)

The latest and state-of-the-art design at freeze, from **early July 2026** (two weeks before the freeze), diagnoses a defect **shared by both prior models** and proposes a fundamentally different fix — a **relabeling**, not just a better annotator:

- **[#6849](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6849)** (rav, 2026-07-02) — "quality classifier sorts documents by domain, not intrinsic quality." On store `store_8ac06c74`: clean `starcoder2/ir_python` code scores ~0.00 (88–99% exactly 0); pristine `cp/arxiv_abstracts` math lands in q0 (0.05–0.20); `multilingual` raw-mean 0.18 vs a type-aware oracle mean 0.51; store bucket q4 is code+math only (0% multilingual/prose).
- **[#6849 follow-up](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6849#issuecomment-4870686601)** — no absolute anchor: within `cp/wikiteam`, q4 "high-quality" docs are still fan-wiki parody cast lists, so "`0.85` means 'excellent arXiv' in one place and 'a fan-wiki parody cast list' in another. Fixing coherence needs an absolute excellence anchor, not just per-type calibration."
- **[#6860](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6860)** (rav, 2026-07-02) — "near-constant scores, no within-source discrimination." `massive_function_calling` = exactly 0.0 for every doc (1 distinct value); synthetic/math saturated high (`nemotron_specialized/math_textbooks` avg 0.968); non-English saturated low (`finepdfs/jpn_Jpan` 0.044); **12 of 98 sources have score stddev < 0.1**.

The **root-cause claim** ([#6849](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6849)): "the Sonnet rubric distills a generic 'pretraining value' target that is ~recoverable from source identity (source alone predicts the oracle at **AUC 0.852**, #6739), so **any faithful distillation reproduces the domain bias — raising oracle-AUC does not fix it**." This is a direct rebuttal of gen-2's premise: gen-2 improved *annotator fidelity against the same defective oracle*, so it inherits the same domain-sorting flaw.

The **validated fix**: a **content-type-aware, source-blind rubric + a pooled ranker**, on branch **`rav/quality-coherence`** at `experiments/datakit/cluster/quality/calibrated/`, lifting **Spearman vs a *new* coherent-quality target from 0.44 → 0.69** and "beats the deployed model on every content type" ([#6849](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6849)). **Note the metrics are not comparable to gen-2's:** 0.44 is the deployed model scored against the *new* coherent-quality relabel; 0.69 is the calibrated ranker against that same new target — not fidelity to the old edu-leaning oracle.

Surfaced as **RFC PR [#7040](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/7040)** (rav, **2026-07-10**), shared the same day in #data-mixing with a public report link, and noted in the 2026-07-14 weekly digest as "an RFC (PR #7040) with a quality classifier report" — **no merge, no deployment** ([Discord 2026-07-10](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1462895580064911522/1525204680509231205); [weekly digest](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1526522772409417788/1526523206725406761)). PR #7040's body is **not in the frozen corpus** (`show` returns "not found in corpus"); every gen-3 number above comes from the #6849/#6860 issue bodies, and the report itself is an external `gs://marin-public` URL (below). Hardware/model-size/FLOPs for the gen-3 ranker are **not stated in-corpus** (gap).

**Path disambiguation:** `quality/v0` = deployed fastText `sonnet46-thr05`; `quality/fast_transformer` = the #6741 offline experiment (adoption pending); `quality/calibrated` (branch `rav/quality-coherence`) = the coherence relabel (RFC stage).

---

## 2. How it was trained

### The oracle & rubric (shared label source for gen-1 and gen-2)

The labels come from an **LLM oracle, not human annotation** ([#5810 run comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5810#issuecomment-4480271122)): **`claude-sonnet-4-6`** scoring documents against a **1–5 pretraining-utility rubric** with a **cached system prompt**; documents are wrapped in `<document>` tags "to prevent the model from completing instruction-tuned docs instead of scoring them." (The issue body hedges "Claude (Sonnet-class)"; the run comment pins it to `claude-sonnet-4-6`.)

Rubric structure (the **verbatim rubric/system-prompt text is not in the frozen corpus** — describe, do not quote):
- Raw 1–5 → `score_normalized ∈ {0, .25, .5, .75, 1.0}`; skewed low (~38% are ≥0.5 "average-or-better") ([#6739 body](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6739)).
- Binary threshold **0.5 normalized = rubric raw ≥ 3** ("Average or better"); train balance **3116 / 1936 (62% / 38%)**. Median Sonnet score landed at raw=2, so a median split would have been ~87% positive — the fixed 0.5 cutoff gives a healthier balance ([#5810 run comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5810#issuecomment-4480271122)).
- Oracle input is **capped at `MAX_TEXT_CHARS = 4000`** — long documents are scored on a ≤4 KB lead ([#6859](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6859)).
- Semantically the oracle is **edu-leaning**: "effectively an educational-value classifier … a near-twin of the FineWeb-Edu / Nemotron-4-edu 0–5 edu rubric," **not** a general-web-quality filter like DCLM ([#6739 methodology note](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6739#issuecomment-4833511462)).

### fastText v0 training (achieved)

- **Sampling**: target **7,000 docs** stratified across the **104 active Datakit sources** (2026-05-18 run), skew-aware via `floor=20 + extra ∝ sqrt(tokens)`; **carve out `safety_pt/*` and `climblab-ja`** (both freshly-added, excluded "to match existing fan-outs"). After **1,387 API/parse failures** (mostly Sonnet rate-limit spikes) → **5,613 usable labels** (train seed=42) ([#5810 run comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5810#issuecomment-4480271122); [#5810 body](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5810)).
- **fastText hyperparameters**: `dim=100, epoch=5, lr=0.5, wordNgrams=2, minCount=3, bucket=200K`; vocab = **67,934**. CPU/API pipeline — no GPU/TPU.
- **Cost / wall clock (achieved vs target)**: **$32.73** ($27.92 train + $4.81 eval) vs a **$50 cap** (the one hard target, met); ~**4.5 h** total wall clock (long pole = all-sources fan-out at 3h04m). Budget-capped and resume-safe by design ([#5810 body](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5810)).
- **Code**: `experiments/datakit/cluster/llm_quality/` (sample → score → train → eval_holdout → eval_vs_dolma3 → all_sources), with a ~$1 smoke test. Deployed the model at the renamed tree location `experiments/datakit/cluster/quality/v0`.
- **Minor internal inconsistency to flag:** usable labels are stated as **5,613**, but the reported train balance 3116 / 1936 sums to **5,052** — a 561-label gap the comment does not explain (note, don't over-weight).

### fast-transformer training (gen-2)

A self-contained **JAX/Equinox `FastTransformer`** trained by **regression** on the same 5,613 oracle-scored docs, evaluated on the same 961 holdout. Ran on a **single TPU v6e-4 slice, region eu-west4, "in minutes"**, launched via the **Iris** v6e pattern (jobs `/power/ft-quality-*`), with **Zephyr** used for the (ultimately unused-for-the-win) nemotron data-prep phase ([#6739 body](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6739); [#6739 report](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6739#issuecomment-4826633470)). Design budget **<1M FLOPs/token achieved at 0.41M**. Per-source score debugging used **ducky/DuckDB** ([#6760](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6760)/[#6762](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6762)); the thread is agent-driven ("weaver #329").

**Every attempt to raise the ceiling with free labels failed** — three independent negatives ([#6739 state](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6739#issuecomment-4833334278), [Phase-1](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6739#issuecomment-4833274655), [FineWeb-Edu](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6739#issuecomment-4833679263)): source-prior pretrain (0.858 < 0.869 scratch), nemotron-bucket (zero-shot ρ 0.28), FineWeb-Edu distillation (zero-shot ρ 0.28). The over-budget NTP outlier (0.877 at 14.7M FLOPs/tok, 14× over budget) did not reproduce (0.858). The team called ~0.87 a **label-quality ceiling** on the 5.6k-doc set — but see §3 for why that framing is now qualified.

---

## 3. How it was evaluated — and why the headline metric is now considered confounded

### The reported numbers (achieved, held-out oracle sample n=961, seed=43)

| Metric | fastText v0 `sonnet46-thr05` | fast-transformer (meanmaxmin·w64·d512·L4) |
|---|---|---|
| AUC | 0.846 | **0.875** |
| Spearman ρ vs oracle | 0.641 | **0.703** |
| Accuracy / F1 | 0.784 / 0.718 | 0.788 / 0.751 |
| FLOPs/token | ~0 | 0.41M (< 1M budget) |
| Params | — | 32M |

([#5810 run comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5810#issuecomment-4480271122); [#6739 final report](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6739#issuecomment-4826633470)). Base rate 39% positive; the fast-transformer's acc/F1 are at a val-calibrated threshold (0.329), since its sigmoid output is compressed; AUC and ρ are threshold-free.

**Side-by-side vs the incumbent `dolma3-fasttext-quality`** on the same 961 docs: ours ρ=**0.641** vs oracle, dolma3 ρ=**0.168**, ours-vs-dolma3 ρ=**0.210** — "~4× better than dolma3 … adding new signal rather than rediscovering it" ([#5810 run comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5810#issuecomment-4480271122)).

### The confound that undercuts these numbers (state-of-the-art view at freeze)

The corpus later establishes that **source identity alone predicts the oracle at AUC 0.852 (η² = 0.41 — source explains 41% of oracle-score variance)**, using per-source mean score with *no text read* ([#6739](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6739#issuecomment-4833103402); corroborated [#6849](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6849)). Two consequences:

1. **The deployed fastText (0.846) sits *below* the source-only ceiling (0.852)** — a lookup of "which of the sources is this" outscores the actual text-reading classifier. Essentially *all* of fastText's oracle-ranking ability is source recoverability.
2. **The fast-transformer's 0.875 clears the source-only ceiling by only ~0.023 AUC** — that thin slice is the maximum attributable to genuine within-source, text-reading quality; the rest (~0.852) is domain/source recoverability. rjpower calls 0.875 the "text-reading plateau" for exactly this reason.

Independent cross-check: FineWeb-Edu's per-doc score predicts the oracle at only ρ 0.28 — "**Source-identity alone (AUC 0.852) predicts our oracle far better than either public edu classifier (0.68)**" ([#6739](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6739#issuecomment-4833679263)).

**So the "0.87 label-quality ceiling" is a ceiling on *annotator fidelity to a confounded, edu-leaning oracle*, not on intrinsic quality.** rjpower's own methodological note ([#6739](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6739#issuecomment-4833511462)): "AUC/ρ-vs-oracle measures annotator fidelity. Because the oracle is edu-leaning, pushing past 0.875 most likely tracks MMLU/ARC and is neutral-to-negative on PIQA/HellaSwag. **The honest test of a quality filter is a small-model data ablation across a CORE-style suite, not oracle-AUC.**" That downstream ablation was **never run** in the corpus — so there is *no* frozen-corpus evidence that any of these classifiers actually improves a trained model's quality; only oracle-fidelity and coherence proxies exist. The gen-3 relabel is the team's response to this whole diagnosis.

### Per-source spot-check caveats (gen-1)

A per-source spot check across all 104 sources ([#5810 spot check](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5810#issuecomment-4481294989)) already foreshadowed the domain bias: multilingual edu content ranked top (Chinese math textbooks mean 0.968, so *not* English-only), "hard-format" sources like `starcoder2/ir_*` and `massive_function_calling` got literally 0.000 mean, a possible English bias inside non-English `finepdfs`, and template-prefix gaming on `nemotron-terminal`. These are the same failure modes later formalized in #6849/#6860.

---

## 4. Source-count / scope drift (do not state a single settled number)

The active-source set **drifted across pipeline layers and dates** and is **never reconciled in the corpus**: **99** in the April registry ([PR #5105](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/5105)) → **104** at the May quality-scored run ([#5810](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5810#issuecomment-4480271122)) → **98** in the July deployed-model bug analysis ([#6860](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6860)) and **114** in the co-partitioned July store `store_8ac06c74` ([#6798](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6798#issuecomment-4883975478)). New sources (e.g. Nemotron Specialized v1.2) were added between May and July. Cite "104" only as the May-run figure, not as a fixed current count.

---

## 5. Can the model weights be shared?

**No explicit release decision exists anywhere in the frozen corpus** — no thread rules yes or no on distributing `model.bin`, and **no Anthropic-terms objection to the classifier is recorded** (genuine gap; RFC PR #7040, the most plausible place such a note would live, is not in-corpus). So the honest answer is: the constraint is **unarticulated in the corpus**. But the corpus contains strong, concrete signals on Marin's revealed preference, and they point toward openness:

**Signals FOR openness (all directly relevant, all in-corpus):**
- **This classifier's own debugging report is already public**, hosted on the world-readable bucket at `https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/rav/quality-score-debugging/2026.07.10.1/index.html`, shared with RFC PR #7040 ([Discord 2026-07-10](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1462895580064911522/1525204680509231205)). `gs://marin-public` is a durable, world-readable public-hosting mechanism by design ([PR #6816](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6816)), so the "internal GCS = not public" framing is undercut for this artifact family.
- **The analogous artifact class is openly released and consumed by Marin**: the dolma3 comparison baseline is AllenAI's openly-released **`allenai/dolma3-fasttext-quality-classifier`** on HuggingFace, pinned at commit `bb89085994fef638ca8dc2ca25169db328e314bb` ([#5812](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5812)) — direct precedent that a fastText document-quality classifier is exactly the kind of thing peers publish openly.
- **Marin keeps its data pool public** on HuggingFace (`marin-community/token-count-viewer`, "23T in our raw pool (pre-dedupe)"; willheld, #data-mixing 2026-07-15, [Discord](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1462895580064911522/1527055120070742037)) and **routinely releases full model weights** (e.g. `marin-community/marin-8b-instruct`).

**The one genuine (but undiscussed) constraint:** the training labels are **distilled entirely from `claude-sonnet-4-6` outputs** (both gen-1 and gen-2), so the artifact's supervision is Claude-derived — the one provenance question a redistribution decision would turn on. **But no message in the corpus raises this as a blocker.**

**On the tangential distillation debate (a caution against over-reading it):** the only "overblown / giant mess" quote in the corpus is a **general debate about LLM distillation attacks**, and it does **not mention the quality classifier at all**. It is **Percy Liang's answer, *relayed* by Colin Raffel** in #questions on 2026-07-15 (Colin: "I recently asked [Percy] … He responded: '…the claims of "it's just distillation" … are kind of overblown, but clearly getting Claude traces is a pretty convenient shortcut … It's a giant mess. 🙂'"), about GLM 5.2 / MAI / Claude-traces for *trained models* — **not** a live channel back-and-forth and **not** about releasing this classifier ([Discord](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1357080963472949428/1527019392821366794)). A parallel willheld message immediately after ("I recently asked @Percy Liang :") is truncated and **not in the corpus** (gap). Do **not** build a "governance tension" for the classifier on this thread — it is off-topic to the artifact.

**Bottom line on sharing:** the corpus records **no decision and no stated policy constraint** specific to the classifier weights. The weights currently sit in the internal working bucket (`gs://marin-eu-west4/datakit/llm-quality-classifier/model/sonnet46-thr05/{model.bin, metadata.json}`), which is where working outputs land — **not** a documented decision to withhold. Everything Marin actually *did* (public report, public pool, open weight-release track record, consuming an openly-released peer classifier) points toward **default-open**; the only real (and unraised) question is the Claude-output provenance of the labels.
